sub_questions: What do RECENTLY ACCEPTED AAAI main-track papers (2024-2026) in ML calibration / uncertainty quantification / selective prediction, and in code-LLM / code generation, actually look like — scope, number of experiments, baselines, models/scale, novelty type, and what reviewers reward vs reject?

Given DPRC's current + projected results (TACO collapse; BigCodeBench per-method oracle 0.931 > scalar 0.875, 32% partial; trained self-expressed AUROC TBD), where does it stand vs that bar — accept / borderline-accept / borderline-reject / reject — and what is the single harshest fair objection?

What specific ADDITIONAL experiments, baselines, ablations, framing, and headline numbers are needed to move DPRC from its current standing to a clear AAAI-27 main-track accept, prioritized by leverage?

Is the competitive-vs-functional contrast (per-requirement confidence collapses on competitive code but is real on functional code) a STRENGTH to lead with (principled scope finding) or a WEAKNESS (reads as narrow/single-benchmark)?
What highest-leverage additions (mechanism/theory result, downstream-utility result, scale/cross-model generalization, human or deployment signal) would most raise acceptance odds — 'cook harder'?

How does DPRC's residual novelty hold against the closest accepted/under-review work (DCPO scalar-on-code; CURE/Atomic per-claim-NL; FLARE/Gros&Devanbu external probes; the UT-Dallas scoop), specifically at the AAAI reviewing bar?
